title: Parameter objects and primitive obsession
summary: Group parameters that travel together, and give primitives a type with rules.

steps.title: Introduce parameter object
body: decimal Revenue(DateTime from, DateTime to, string region) { ... }
int Orders(DateTime from, DateTime to, string region) { ... }
string Report(DateTime from, DateTime to, string region) { ... }
`from, to, region` is a **data clump**. Each method repeats the same parameters, and each probably repeats the same check that `from <= to`. **Introduce Parameter Object**:
record ReportQuery(DateTime From, DateTime To, string Region);
A bonus appears right away: behaviour that belongs to the clump (`q.Contains(date)`, `q.Days`) now has a home.

steps.prompt: Which parameter list is the strongest candidate for a parameter object?
options: `(double lat, double lon)` appearing in twelve methods
`(int count, bool verbose)` in one method

steps.title: Primitive obsession
body: Primitives (`string`, `int`, `decimal`) carry no rules. A `string email` might be `""`. A `decimal price` might be negative or in the wrong currency. An `int userId` and `int orderId` can be swapped without the compiler noticing:
Refund(user.Id, order.Id);          // compiles, and is wrong
Add validation in the constructor, and every `Email` in the program is a valid email.

steps.prompt: Primitive obsession, or a primitive that is fine?
items: `int orderId` and `int userId` side by side
`bool verbose` flag for a CLI tool

code: record ReportQuery(DateTime From, DateTime To, string Region);
decimal Revenue(__1__ query) => Sales(query.__2__).Where(s => s.At >= query.From && s.At <= query.__3__).Sum(s => s.Amount);

steps.title: Introduce a parameter object
prompt: `Overlaps` and `Nights` both take `checkIn, checkOut` pairs. Introduce `record Stay(DateOnly CheckIn, DateOnly CheckOut)` with:
- `bool Overlaps(Stay other)` (a stay ending on the day another starts does **not** overlap)
- the constructor throws `ArgumentException` unless `CheckOut` is after `CheckIn`
starter: int Nights(DateOnly checkIn, DateOnly checkOut) => checkOut.DayNumber - checkIn.DayNumber;
bool Overlaps(DateOnly checkInA, DateOnly checkOutA, DateOnly checkInB, DateOnly checkOutB) =>
solution: if (checkOut <= checkIn) throw new ArgumentException("check-out must be after check-in");
public bool Overlaps(Stay other) => CheckIn < other.CheckOut && other.CheckIn < CheckOut;
template: var dojoA = new Stay(new DateOnly(2025, 6, 1), new DateOnly(2025, 6, 4));
Dojo.Eq("overlapping stays", true, dojoA.Overlaps(new Stay(new DateOnly(2025, 6, 3), new DateOnly(2025, 6, 6))));
Dojo.Eq("back-to-back stays do not overlap", false, dojoA.Overlaps(new Stay(new DateOnly(2025, 6, 4), new DateOnly(2025, 6, 5))));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("zero nights is refused", () => new Stay(new DateOnly(2025, 6, 1), new DateOnly(2025, 6, 1)));

forbid.message: The old four-parameter method is gone

steps.title: Replace the primitive
prompt: Emails are `string`s, checked (or not) all over the place. Write `readonly record struct Email`:
- constructor `Email(string value)`: trims, lower-cases, and throws `ArgumentException` unless there is exactly one `@` with text on both sides
- `string Value { get; }`, `string Domain` (the part after `@`), and `ToString()` returning `Value`
template: Dojo.Eq("equal by value", new Email("a@b.c"), new Email("A@B.C"));
